newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies end up, gains pared ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies end up, gains pared ahead of data.

text.p: CME pork belly futures finished sharply higher but closing values were well off limit gains posted in some months during the session as traders awaited the USDA's Cold Storage Report. Hog futures tumbled for losses as they lacked support from bellies late, traders said.

Pork bellies closed 1.325 to 2.300 cents per lb higher with July up 1.500 at 90.550 cents. May, February and March briefly posted 3.000-cent limit gains before slipping. Hog futures ended 0.675 cent per lb lower to unchanged with June pacing the loss at 80.825 cents.
Mixed profit taking and local liquidation weighed on pork bellies after early demand in front of the report, they said.

Estimates by some market watchers that the USDA data would show that bellies were moved out of storage in April rather than the more-typical scenario where bellies are put into storage ahead of peak summer demand, took futures up sharply.

Indications on Tuesday's monthly Cold Storage report ranged from 52.2 million to 59 million lbs in U.S. warehouses on May 1 compared with 54.8 million on hand April 1 and 57.2 million in storage May 1 of last year. Net storings estimates ranged from out 2.64 to in 4.16 million lbs and compared with the 10-year average net-in product movement of 9.8 million lbs.

Estimates on the CME's weekly Out-of-Town Report ranged from in 250,000 to 1.0 million lbs of bellies into warehouses outside Chicago versus in-movement of 836,000 lbs last week and in-movement of 2.482 million lbs last year.
After the close, the CME reported a net in-movement of 912,000 lbs.
R.J. O'Brien, ING and Dean Witter were notable early buyers while locals sold late, pit sources said.

Hog futures turned lower when pork belly gains were rebuffed and weak wholesale pork prices weighed on trade sentiment. Long liquidation and rolling of June longs into August added to pressure in nearby June, traders said.

Disappointment was evident when the rally from recent losses was not more substantial, some sources noted. Expectations of steady to weak cash hog prices Wednesday, as packer demand for hogs should ease ahead of the holiday and short kill week next week, also weighed on prices, they said.
Recent light hog marketings and discount of futures to the CME lean hog index provided only light early support.
Latest lean index was down $0.42 to $84.03 per cwt.
Rand Financials sold June late while R.J. O'Brien sold July, traders said, and Prudential sold August and October.
Cargill Investor Services spread long August/short June early. In hog options, Refco bought October 72 calls early, pit sources said.
